newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South Africa says willing to send troops to Zaire.
newsitem.headline: South Africa says willing to send troops to Zaire.

text.p: President Nelson Mandela said on Monday he was prepared to send South African troops to Central Africa as part of an international force to bring peace to war-torn eastern Zaire.
"In principle, I am prepared to contribute troops," Mandela said in a joint television interview with South Africa's state broadcaster and CNN.
Mandela said he would send a delegation to the Great Lakes region to gather information that would allow him to decide how big a unit to commit.
His goversment has said it would be prepared to take part in a humanitarian effort in Central Africa, but Monday's comments were the first from the president that referred to committing troops.

Mandela, who had so far resisted military intervention in any African crises, said he had given the undertaking to former Tanzanian president Julius Nyerere, who visited South Africa at the weekend to discuss the ongoing crisis in Central Africa.

Nyerere briefed Mandela on a summit of East and Central African leaders who decided last week that a neutral force should be created to provide safe corridors for aid to more than a million refugees from ethnic violence in Rwanda and Burundi.
It would be intended to help Rwandan refugees now in eastern Zaire to return to their home country.

The U.N. Security Council called on U.N. members at the weekend to lay the groundwork for a multinational force to help feed the region torn apart by fighting between rebels and Zairean government forces.
Last week South Africa decided to suspend an 87 million rand ($18.5 million) arms contract with the Rwandan government because of the fighting in the region.
